questions.question: Which of the following statements is NOT correct regarding laterite soil?

options.text: Red laterite soils in Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh and Kerala are more suitable for crops like cashew nut.
They are generally rich in humus.
This soil is very useful for growing tea and coffee.
The laterite soil develops in areas with high temperature and heavy rainfall.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Option 2**__. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **They are generally rich in humus**: This statement is NOT correct.
 
• **Laterite soils are generally low in fertility and organic matter, including humus.**
 
• They are often leached of essential nutrients due to heavy rainfall and have a low capacity to retain organic matter.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Red laterite soils in Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, and Kerala** **are more suitable for crops like cashew nut: **Red laterite soils found in these regions have good drainage properties and are rich in iron and aluminum oxides.

 
 
• These soil characteristics make them suitable for crops like **cashew nut**, which thrive in well-drained soils.
 
 
 
• **This soil is very useful for growing tea and coffee:** Laterite soils are suitable for growing tea and coffee.
 
 
• These crops require well-drained soils with good water-holding capacity, and the characteristics of laterite soils, such as their ability to retain moisture, make them conducive to tea and coffee cultivation.
 
 
 
• **The laterite soil develops in areas with high temperature and heavy rainfall: **Laterite soils are primarily found in tropical and subtropical regions with high temperatures and heavy rainfall.
 
 
• The intense weathering and leaching processes that occur in these regions contribute to the formation of laterite soils.

questions.question: The total pressure of a mixture of ideal gases is the sum of partial pressures. This is ______ law of partial pressures.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 1**__. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• This is known as Dalton's law of partial pressures.
 
• According to Dalton's law, the total pressure exerted by a mixture of non-reacting ideal gases is equal to the sum of the partial pressures of each individual gas.
 
• Dalton's law is based on the assumption that the gases in the mixture behave independently of one another, without any significant interactions or reactions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Boyle's Law:**

 
 
• Boyle's law states that, at a constant temperature, the volume of a given amount of gas is inversely proportional to its pressure.
 
• In other words,** as the pressure of a gas increases, its volume decreases, and vice versa, provided the temperature remains constant.** Mathematically, Boyle's law can be expressed as:
 
• **P₁V₁ = P₂V₂**
 
• where** P₁ and V₁ **are the** initial pressure** and **volume**, and **P₂ and V₂** are the **final pressure and volume**, respectively.
 
 
 
• **Charles's Law:**
 
 
• **Charles's law** states that, at a constant pressure, the volume of a given amount of gas is directly proportional to its absolute temperature. This means that as the temperature of a gas increases, its volume also increases, and as the temperature decreases, its volume decreases, as long as the pressure remains constant. Mathematically, Charles's law can be expressed as:
 
• **V₁/T₁ = V₂/T₂**
 
• where **V₁ and T₁ **are the initial **volume and temperature (in Kelvin), **and** V₂ and T₂ **are the **final volume and temperature**, respectively.
 
 
 
• **Avogadro's Law:**
 
 
• **Avogadro's law states** that, at a constant temperature and pressure, equal volumes of gases contain an equal number of particles (atoms, molecules, or ions).
 
• This law implies that the volume of a gas is directly proportional to the number of moles of gas present. Mathematically, Avogadro's law can be expressed as:
 
• **V₁/n₁ = V₂/n₂**
 
 

where** V₁ and n₁ **are the** initial volume** and number of** moles**, and **V₂ and n₂** are the **final volume **and number of **moles,** respectively.

questions.question: The important system components like the central processing unit (CPU) and random access memory (RAM) modules are connected directly to the ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 2**__. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The important system components like the** central processing unit (CPU)** and **random access memory (RAM) **modules are connected directly to the **Motherboard.**
 
• **The motherboard** acts as the** main circuit board** of a **computer system,** providing electrical connections and pathways for various hardware components to communicate with each other.
 
• **The CPU i**s typically inserted into a socket on the motherboard, and the **RAM **modules are installed into slots on the motherboard.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Magnetic Tape:** Magnetic tape is a medium used for long-term storage of data.

 
 
• It is typically used for backup purposes rather than directly connecting components like **CPU and RAM.**
 
• Magnetic tape drives are separate devices that connect to a computer system.
 
 
 
• **Optical Disk: **An optical disk is a storage medium that uses laser technology to read and write data.
 
 
• Examples of optical disks include **CDs, DVDs, and Blu-ray discs**.
 
• While optical drives can be connected to the motherboard, they are used primarily for reading and writing data from optical disks rather than directly connecting the** CPU and RAM.**
 
 
 
• **Flash memory** is a type of **non-volatile memory** that retains data even when power is removed.
 
 
• It is commonly used in **USB flash drives**, **solid-state drives (SSDs),** and **memory cards.**
 
• **Flash memory **can be connected to the **motherboard** through various interfaces such as** USB, SATA, or PCIe**.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements is correct regarding the direct taxes?

I. Levied on taxable income earned by individuals and corporate entities.

II. Gift tax is a type of direct tax.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Option 3**__**.** 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Both statements are correct regarding **direct taxes**:

 
 
• **Direct taxes** are levied on** taxable income** earned by individuals and corporate entities.
 
• Examples of direct taxes include** income tax, corporate tax, and wealth tax**.
 
• These taxes are directly imposed on the income or wealth of individuals and entities.
 
• **Gift tax** is indeed a type of direct tax.
 
• It is a tax imposed on the transfer of property or assets as a gift from one individual to another.
 
• The person giving the gift (donor) is usually responsible for paying the tax, although in some cases, the recipient may be liable for reporting the gift.
 
• **Gift tax **is considered a **direct tax** because it is directly imposed on the transfer of property or assets.

questions.question: Before writing codes in a high level language, a ______ of a program helps in representing the basic functionality of the intended program.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**pseudocode**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Pseudocode:**

 
 
• Pseudocode is a high-level description of a program that uses plain language or a simplified syntax to outline the logic and structure of the intended code.
 
• It allows programmers to focus on the algorithmic steps without getting bogged down by the syntax of a specific programming language.
 
 
 
• **Original code:**
 
 
• This option refers to the actual code written in a high-level language.
 
• It is the final implementation of the program, which is executed by the computer.
 
• While original code is essential for executing the program, it is not the most suitable choice for representing the basic functionality of the program before writing actual code.
 
 
 
• **Small code:**
 
 
• "Small code" is not a commonly used term in programming.
 
• It is vague and does not specifically describe any stage or representation of a program.
 
 
 
• **Naïve code:**
 
 
• "Naïve code" is also not a standard term in programming.
 
• It could refer to code written by a novice programmer, which may lack efficiency or optimization.
 
• However, it does not represent a stage or technique used to represent the basic functionality of a program.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is **NOT **correct regarding sound?

options.text: In human beings, the vibration of vocal cords produces sound.

questions.solution:
Correct Answer **Sound can travel through vacuum**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points:__**__Concept:__

__
 
• A sound is a form of energy that produces the sensation of hearing in our ears.
 
• Sound is a type of longitudinal wave.
 
• Sound is measured in Decibels(Db).
 
• The speed of the sound varies in different mediums.

Explanation:__

__
 
• Sound from a violin and a flute played at the same time travel at the same speed.
 
 
• Both sounds travel through the same medium which is air.
 
• Both the sounds travel through at the same speed at the same time but the sound we receive are different due to characteristics associated with the sound such as pitch and amplitude.
 
• Hence, option 1 is correct.
 
 
 
• Two sound waves of the same intensity would not be perceived to have the same loudness because of the human's ear tendency to amplify sounds having frequencies in the range from 10kHz to 50kHz, sounds with these intensities seem louder to the human ear. Hence, option 2 is incorrect.
 
• Speed of sound in hot air is more than that of the room temperature because heat makes air molecules move around faster. Hence, option 3 is correct.
 
• The speed of sound depends on the density of the material.
 
 
• Tightly packed material molecules transfer the sound at high speed.
 
• Speed of sound is fastest in Solids, Liquids then Gas.
 
 

Thus, the incorrect statement is that two sound waves of the same intensity will always have equal loudness. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**Amplitude:

__
 
• Amplitude is the measure of compression or rarefaction of particles of a medium through which sound is traveling.
 
• The higher the amplitude, the louder the sound.
 
• The amplitude A is related to loudness as loudness ∝ A2

Frequency:

 
• Frequency refers to the rate of vibration of sound.
 
• The pitch of a sound is decided by the measure of frequency.
 
• The higher the frequency, the shriller the sound.
 
• Frequency measured in Hertz (Hz).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__ Sound in the air: 

 
• In a gas-like air, the particles are generally far apart so they travel further before they bump into one another.
 
• There is not much resistance to movement so it doesn’t take much to start a wave, but it won’t travel as fast.

Sound in water:

 
• In water, the particles are much closer together, and they can quickly transmit vibrational energy from one particle to the next.
 
• This means that the sound wave travels over four times faster than it would in the air, but it takes a lot of energy to start the vibration.

Sound in solids: 

 
• In a solid, the particles are even closer together and linked by chemical bonds so the wave travels even faster than it does in either liquid or air, but you need quite a lot of energy to start the wave at the beginning.

questions.question: The northern plains of India are formed up of which soil?
questions.solution:
Correct Answer is **Alluvial**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points:__****Northern Plains:**

__
 
• The great Northern Plains have been formed by alluvium deposits brought by rivers flowing from the Himalayas and the Great Indian Plateau.
 
• This plain is dead flat, with almost negligible slope.
 
• The plain is of two types Bangar and khadar.
 
• The Great Northern Plain can be divided into four parts - Western Plain, North Central Plain, Eastern Plain, and Brahmaputra Plain. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Red Soil: Red soil develops on crystalline igneous rocks in areas of low rainfall in the eastern and southern parts of the Deccan Plateau.
 
• Laterite Soil: The laterite soils develop in areas with high temperatures and high rainfall.
 
• Black Soil: Black soil covers most of the Deccan Plateau which includes parts of Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh, Gujarat, Andhra Pradesh, and some parts of Tamil Nadu.

questions.question: In ______ the Muslim League had moved a resolution demanding “Independent States” for Muslims in the north-western and eastern areas of the country
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __1940.__

__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points:__**

__
 
• The Muslim League advocated autonomy for the areas of the subcontinent with a majority of Muslims, which were the geographically adjacent territories in the North-West and the East, in its 1940 Resolution.
 
• These were to be "independent states," with full autonomy and sovereignty.
 
• However, at this time, neither the concept of a formal "Pakistan" nor the ambiguity of their decision spoke to any kind of separation.
 
• It ultimately led to the partition of India in 1947 by the British Empire.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information:__**

 
• All India Muslim League was founded in 1906 to safeguard the rights of Indian Muslims.
 
• Founders: Muhammad Ali Jinnah, Aga Khan III, Hakim Ajmal Khan, Khwaja Salimullah, Waqar-ul-Mulk
 
• Founded: 30 December 1906

questions.question: In India, Who was appointed the new Chief of Defence Staff (CDS) in September 2022?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __Anil Chauhan__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points:__**

__
 
• The Government announced Lt General Anil Chauhan (retired) as the new CDS.
 
• He is the second CDS of India. ​
 
• General Anil Chauhan, PVSM, UYSM, AVSM, SM, and VSM assumed office as the Chief of Defence Staff (CDS) on September 30, 2022.

 [IMAGE: https://images.moneycontrol.com/static-mcnews/2022/09/aatf71ko_new-cds-anil-chauhan-ndtv-650_650x400_28_September_22-707x435.png?impolicy=website&width=770&height=431] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information:__**

 
• ​The Chief of Defence Staff (CDS) is the military head and acts as the single-point advisor to the Government of India in matters of India’s military.
 
• He is also the permanent Chairman of the Chiefs of Staff Committee (CoSC) of the Indian Armed Forces.
 
• The Chief also heads the Department of Military Affairs.
 
• The first Chief of Defence Staff, General Bipin Rawat took office on 1 January 2020.
 
• The creation of the post of CDS was first recommended after the 1999 Kargil War.
